title: Sort Array By Parity II
statement:
The array `nums` has an even length, and exactly half of its values are even while the other half are odd. Rearrange the values so that every even index holds an even number and every odd index holds an odd number, then return the rearranged array.

Many arrangements meet this rule; any one of them is accepted. You may reorder `nums` in place and return it, or return a new array with the same values.
constraints: Exactly half of the values in nums are even
notes:
## Intuition

Building two lists (evens and odds) and interleaving them is easy but uses O(n) extra space. In place, notice that the misplaced values come in pairs: if an even slot holds an odd number, then some odd slot must hold an even number, because each parity fills exactly half the array. Swapping those two fixes both at once.

## Approach

1. Keep a pointer `odd` on the odd indices, starting at `1`.
2. Walk `even` over the even indices `0, 2, 4, ...`.
3. If `nums[even]` is already even, move on.
4. Otherwise advance `odd` by 2 until it lands on an odd slot holding an even number.
5. Swap `nums[even]` and `nums[odd]`. Both slots are now correct.
6. Return `nums`.

Both pointers only move forward, so the slots `odd` has passed are already correct and never need another look.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4, 2, 5, 7]`. At `even = 0` the value `4` is even, so skip. At `even = 2` the value `5` is odd. `odd = 1` holds `2`, which is even, so the loop does not move it. Swap positions 2 and 1 to get `[4, 5, 2, 7]`. The answer is `[4, 5, 2, 7]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `even` and `odd` each cross the array once.
- Space: O(1): the swaps happen inside `nums`.

## Pitfalls

- Advance `odd` in steps of 2, not 1, or it will wander onto even slots.
- `odd` must persist across iterations; restarting it at 1 makes the method O(n²).
- The search for a misplaced even value cannot run off the end: the counts guarantee one exists whenever an even slot holds an odd number.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `even` | the even index being checked |
| `odd` | the next odd index that may hold a misplaced even number |
| `temp` | holds a value during the swap |

narration.2: The odd-slot pointer starts at the first odd index.
narration.4: Visit the even indices from left to right.
narration.5: An even number in an even slot is already fine.
narration.6: Skip to the next even slot.
narration.8: This even slot holds an odd number, so look for an odd slot holding an even number.
narration.9: Odd slots that already hold odd numbers are correct; jump over them two at a time.
narration.11: Save the misplaced odd number before the swap.
narration.12: Put the even number from the odd slot into the even slot.
narration.13: Put the odd number into the odd slot; both slots are now correct.
narration.15: Every even slot holds an even number, so every odd slot holds an odd one too.
